subject: Re: Follow-up: Feature parity & competitive eval next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coale@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T15:10:00Z
Subject: Post-demo recap & next steps (feature parity + tests)

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the Acme team today. Thanks for walking through your priority use cases (in-product assistance, multi-step tool orchestration, and real-time streaming summaries). Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed next steps so we can move the competitive evaluation forward quickly.

Summary of asks from your side:
- Feature parity checks vs your current providers (hyperscaler inference & existing API) for: function/tool calling, structured outputs (JSON schema enforcement), and streaming latency/quality.
- A short, repeatable test plan we can run together against our hosted API and provide results you can validate.
- Clarify success criteria: maximum tail latency for streaming, accuracy of structured outputs (schema validation rate), and any cost targets.

What we (Redwood) will deliver by Friday (2026-06-26):
1) A concise test plan with concrete test vectors and expected success criteria (attached: acme-feature-parity-test-plan.pdf).
2) Short-term access for your engineering team to our sandbox endpoint for 3 specific tests (function calling, structured outputs, real-time streaming). We can provide API keys scoped to the tests.
3) A side-by-side comparison matrix showing capability differences and recommended next tests — we’ll call out what’s due to runtime (latency/streaming) vs model behavior.

Immediate asks for you:
- Confirm the success criteria (latency targets and schema validation thresholds) or propose edits to the attached plan.
- Share who on your side will run the tests (email + preferred Slack handle) so we can provision sandbox keys.

Attachments: acme-feature-parity-test-plan.pdf (test vectors + scoreboard), recording-20260622.mp4 (demo recording).

Thanks — I’ll set up the sandbox credentials once you confirm the test owners.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.coale@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coale@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T18:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap & next steps (feature parity + tests)

Thanks Marissa — solid recap and appreciate the quick turnaround. Laura (engineering lead) and I reviewed the test plan; a couple quick clarifications: 

1) Success criteria: for streaming, 95th percentile end-to-end token latency should be <= 350ms for sessions with avg seq length ~256; for structured outputs, we want >= 98% schema conformance across our 150 validation prompts. For function/tool calling, we care about deterministic argument extraction and confidence scores that we can threshold.

2) Test owners: I’ll run the structured outputs and tool-calling tests (alex.johnson@acme.com, Slack: @alexj). Laura will run the streaming tests (laura.chen@acme.com, Slack: @laura).

3) Can you confirm whether the sandbox keys will allow streaming with chunked responses (server-sent events) and function-call hooks? Our current vendor uses SSE for streaming, and we rely on immediate tool-trigger callbacks.

If Redwood can confirm SSE + function hooks in the sandbox, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Laura next week.

Alex
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coale@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T09:12:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo recap & next steps (feature parity + tests)

Folks — forwarding Alex’s notes. Key asks we need to operationalize:
- Confirm sandbox supports SSE-style streaming and function-call hooks with the same semantics we demo’d.
- Provision scoped API keys for alex.johnson@acme.com and laura.chen@acme.com for the three tests. Keys should be time-limited (7 days) and rate-limited to the test plan volumes.
- Run an internal smoke test for the structured output vectors and share a baseline within 24 hours so Alex has something to compare.

Dev — can you handle provisioning and the internal smoke run? Vivek — please prepare a short comparison note highlighting any known deltas vs hyperscalers around SSE behavior and function-calling determinism so we can be transparent.

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the kickoff meeting once keys are ready.

Marissa

> Hi Alex — great to meet you and the Acme team today. Thanks for walking through your priority use cases (in-product assistance, multi-step tool orchestration, and real-time streaming summaries). Per our call, I wanted to capture the agreed next steps so we can move the competitive evaluation forward quickly.

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.coale@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-demo recap & next steps (feature parity + tests)

Marissa — I can take this. Plan:
1) Provision two time-limited sandbox API keys (7-day TTL) for Alex and Laura by EOD 2026-06-24. Keys will be scoped to: text generation, streaming (SSE), function-calling endpoints, and schema validation helper.
2) Run quick smoke tests against the structured output vectors in the attached plan. I’ll post a short baseline report (CSV summary + quick notes) to the Drive link and paste the snapshot here. Expect baseline by 2026-06-25 18:00 UTC.
3) Vivek, can you assemble the comparison note on SSE and function hook determinism? If you can include known behavioral diffs vs Bedrock/Vertex/OpenAI, that will help Alex prioritize.

Also: streaming in our hosted sandbox uses chunked SSEs; function hooks are supported via a webhook callback model (we send a signed callback request to your provided endpoint when a function call is emitted). There is a small difference vs some hyperscalers: we provide an option to return function-call arguments as a validated JSON payload (helpful for strict schema enforcement) vs free-form text. Will note this in the comparison doc.

Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.coale@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:35:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Feature parity & competitive eval next steps

Alex/Laura — quick status update and proposed timeline: 

- Sandbox keys provisioned (7-day TTL). You should have received two emails with credentials and usage notes; let me know if not and I’ll re-send.
- Internal baseline for structured outputs: we ran the 150 validation prompts against Redwood host with our recommended model + quantization profile. Preliminary schema conformance: 97.1% (we’ve flagged the ~2.9% for root-cause — most are edge-cases with nested optional fields). Full CSV is in the Drive link.

- SSE + function hooks: confirmed supported. Dev’s note: we support chunked SSEs and webhook callbacks; we can optionally return function arguments as validated JSON to match strict schema expectations.

Next steps / proposed 7-day plan (starting today):
1) Acme runs the three tests (structured outputs, function calling, streaming) by 2026-07-01.
2) Redwood will ingest results and provide a side-by-side scoreboard and a short write-up highlighting where differences stem from the model vs runtime within 48 hours after results are received.
3) If you want, we can schedule a 45-min review with engineering next week to walk the scoreboard and recommended mitigations (quant profiles, batching tweaks).

If that timeline works, I’ll schedule the review and open a HubSpot activity. Also, if Acme is comfortable with the results and wants to move ahead, I can send initial contract paperwork / PO process (DocuSign link) — Alex, flag if procurement should be looped in earlier.

Thanks — looking forward to the tests.

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.coale@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
